back_translation: In the reign of Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram, with Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, marched up to Jerusalem to wage war against the city, but they could not prevail.
When someone reported to the house of David, "Aram has encamped in Ephraim," the royal heart of Ahaz and the hearts of his people shook, as trees of the forest shake before a storm wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah: "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and Shear-jashub your son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field,

and tell him: 'Be careful and stay calm. Do not fear and do not let your heart be timid because of these two stubs of smoldering firewood — because of the blazing anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.
For Aram, with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted harm against you, saying:
"Let us go up and attack Judah, make it cower in dread, then seize and divide it among ourselves, and install the son of Tabeal as king there."
But the Lord GOD says this: "That plan will not succeed, and it will not come to pass.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered until it is no longer a people.
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not believe firmly, you will not be firmly established at all."'"
The LORD spoke to Ahaz again:
"Ask for a sign from the LORD your God — let it be as deep as the realm of the dead or as high as heaven above."
But Ahaz replied: "We will not ask, and we will not test the LORD."
Then Isaiah said: "Hear now, O house of David! Is it too small a thing for you to weary men, that you would also weary the heart of my God?
Therefore the Sovereign Master will give you a sign Himself: Behold, the virgin will conceive and bear a son, and she will call his name Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey until he knows to refuse evil and choose good.
For before the boy knows to refuse evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be left abandoned.
The LORD will bring upon you, upon your people, and upon your father's royal house days such as have never come since the day Ephraim broke away from Judah — namely, the king of Assyria."
In that day the LORD will whistle with His lips to call the swarm of biting flies from the farthest streams of Egypt, and to call the swarm of bees from the land of Assyria.
They will all come and settle in the steep ravines, in the clefts of the rocks, on every thornbush, and at every watering place.

In that day the Sovereign Master will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates River — namely, the king of Assyria — to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and it will sweep away your beard as well.
In that day a man will only manage to keep alive one young cow and two sheep.
And because of the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for everyone left in the midst of the land will eat curds and honey.
In that day, every place that once had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver will become a place of briers and thornbushes.
A man will be able to enter there only carrying bow and arrows, for the whole land will be full of briers and thornbushes.
As for all the hills once tilled with the hoe, you will not go there for fear of the briers and thornbushes; they will become a place to turn cattle loose and a trampling ground for sheep.
